text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: latency spike detected on /v1/generate (p95 ~ 4800ms) across us-west-2; paging on-call

maria: I'm on it, grabbing traces and the recent deploys. Any customer-facing errors?

ashwin: seeing error rate flat, just latency. A few 503s from backend cache timeouts but <0.1%

eli: jumping in — routing traces to temp-s3 and will paste links. Holding canary traffic off via feature-flag.

incident-bot: On-call: @sre-rotations (rotation: ashwin) has been paged

ashwin: thanks. timeline so far: 13:02 prod: minor kernel patch rolled to a subset of nodes in pool-gpu-03; 13:07 we started seeing p95 drift; 13:12 alerts fired

maria: customer-impact: some interactive workloads in Hosted API (small-PSU customers) experienced 3-6s tail latency. CS notified for two support tickets (ids #4522, #4523).

jason: mitigating: I've scaled dedicated fallback pool and forced traffic to pool-gpu-01/02. Rolling routing change now (2m).

eli: logs: past 30s from a slow request trace (span names + perf counters):
```
TRACE_ID: 8f2c1a
spans:
 - decode_tokens (30ms)
 - attention_kv (p50 120ms p95 3.1s)
 - aten::matmul (gpu 180ms)
 - kvcache_lookup (p95 2.9s)
perf_counters:
 - context_switches: +180
 - cpu_preemptions: elevated
 - syscall_latency_us: 2100
```

maria: interesting that attention_kv and kvcache_lookup are huge. Could be kernel-level preemption or NVMe I/O stall? Which nodes had kernel patch applied?

ashwin: only pool-gpu-03 had the kernel update (linux:5.15 -> 5.15.73 backported preempt change). I can correlate node list.

observability-bot: Snapshot created: s3://redwood-traces/2412009876/trace-8f2c1a.json (note: contains full spans + counters)

ashwin: quick check: rolling routing lowered p95 in 2/3 affected colocations. After shifting ~40% traffic off pool-gpu-03, p95 dropped from ~4.8s to ~1.2s for those flows.

maria: ask: are we confident the kernel change triggered standstills? Any evidence of increased syscalls or preemptions?

eli: from perf counters aggregated (10s windows) on affected hosts:
```
host: gpu-03-a
 - cpu_context_switches: 420/s (baseline 60/s)
 - softirqs: elevated (net_rx 3x)
 - nvme_io_wait_ms: spikes 1500ms
```

ashwin: NVMe I/O wait is suspicious — we saw similar symptoms when kernel backport changed block layer scheduler in earlier patch. Could be interplay between preemptible kernel and IO scheduler leading to long syscall waits causing user threads to block and starve GPU helper threads (KV cache driver).

jason: mitigation note: scaled fallback + routing change reduced customer impact; recommend draining pool-gpu-03 and reboots to previous kernel until patch validated.

maria: @ops can you coordinate drain + revert patch on pool-gpu-03? Put an explicit canary after revert.

ops: on it. starting cordon/drain of gpu-03 nodes now. ETA for full drain 12m. Will revert kernel after confirming node is out of rotation.

customer-success: I notified affected customers with temporary mitigation note; offering credit if latency persists.

eli: tracking hypotheses inline: H1: kernel preempt/blk scheduler change -> increased syscall latency -> KV cache lockups -> p95 spike. H2: NVMe firmware hiccup coincident with kernel -> IO waits increase. H3: workload pattern shifted (longer sequence lengths) causing KV cache churn (less likely given consistent traffic profiles).

maria: good. Let's collect data to test H1/H2. Actions: (A1) gather perf counters and ftrace from gpu-03 hosts (ashwin), (A2) collect NVMe SMART and kernel logs (ops), (A3) run synthetic replay on a patched host with probe instrumentation (eli). Put results back here.

ashwin: A1 done for first window, uploading: s3://redwood-metrics/2412009876/perf_window_1309.csv

ops: A2: NVMe SMART shows reallocated sectors stable, but controller reported transient media_wait events at 13:05 on 03-b. kernel logs attached in s3: s3://redwood-logs/2412009876/gpu-03-kern.log

eli: A3: synthetic replay on patched host reproduced p95 ~3.4s with kvcache lookup stalls. When we switched to nohz=off (reduces scheduler tick handling), p95 dropped to ~1.1s in the replay. Suggests scheduler/tick/preempt interactions.

maria: great repro. That points strongly to H1. But we should still validate with NVMe firmware check.

jason: ops has reverted kernel on one drained host (03-a) and placed back into pool. Monitoring now.

incident-bot: Update: pool-gpu-03 nodes are draining (3/6); routing change in effect; p95 for /v1/generate global now trending to 850ms from 4.8s at peak.

ashwin: added a short perf script to capture ctx switch + preempt counts every 5s for next 10m across hosts. Link: s3://redwood-metrics/2412009876/preempt_counts.csv

ops: reverted kernel across all drained nodes and reintroduced them one by one. No NVMe firmware updates pending.

eli: re-run of synthetic replay on reverted kernel hosts shows baseline p95 ~220ms, no spike. Re-run on patched kernel host still shows ~3s p95.

maria: conclusion for immediate mitigation: revert kernel and drain+reboot patched hosts. Customer impact mitigated and CS notified.

ashwin: next steps for RCA: collect full ftrace for preempt events, bisect kernel patch list to the specific commit, check blk-mq scheduler flags, and coordinate with infra kernel patch authors. I'll open an internal ticket and assign owners.

maria: I'll draft customer-facing RCA once we confirm root cause commit. For thread: keep this as the incident record and update with artifacts.

jason: postmortem notes to add: timeline, mitigation steps, evidence (traces + perf + synthetic repro), recommended gating for kernel patches (perf regression tests on our replay harness), and rollback plan for future.

observability-bot: Saved timeline snapshot: s3://redwood-postmortems/2412009876/timeline.json

maria: handing off to oncall for follow-up analysis; @ashwin and @eli will be primary investigators for RCA. I'll close the paging after final confirm.

sre-rotations: taking handoff. Will coordinate bisect and liaise with kernel team. Adding tasks to the RCA ticket.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Paging cleared for now.

maria: thanks everyone. Please keep adding links to artifacts here. We'll schedule a 30m sync if needed. :thumbsup:
